numeral.purpose: Weight and reps on the current set; steps down to 60, 48 and 40px as the number gets longer.

figure.purpose: The best set on an exercise-history session plate.

heading.purpose: Week, part and month titles (900); done and waiting set values (700); rest time left.

row.purpose: Bar-button labels (900), list row names and part counts (700).

body.purpose: Running text and field rows; 900 only for the active pair segment and alert titles.

note.purpose: Quiet units, tips, notes, set titles on the accent plate.

meta.purpose: Set titles, meta lines, pills, section line.

caption.purpose: Weekday letters, rail cells, list footers, the live clock.

narrative.overview:
The app reads like Israeli highway signage seen from a moving car: heavy Hebrew type on outlined plates, over asphalt grey, legible in one glance from arm's length. The owner uses it mid-set on an iPhone SE, one-handed, between sets; every screen is drawn at 375×647 first and judged on the phone. The sign world lends type, palette, density and one signature move, the keyline plate. Navigation, sheets, swipe-back and the tab bar stay iOS-standard (Ionic forced to iOS mode).

Density is low and deliberate. Each record, set, routine or session is its own plate; the one thing that matters on a plate gets the owner's accent as a fill, with near-black ink text and an ink ring just inside the edge. Real buttons sit under the thumb in the lower half: outlined 48px steppers and full-width bars, never bare glyphs. The world rejects the dark card holding a set table, thin poster numerals, and flat colour tiles (the replaced "Type tiles" look).
keyCharacteristics: Always dark: charcoal ground, graphite plates, 2px keylines, 14px corners.
Heebo at 500, 700 and 900 only; numbers are heavy and units quiet.
One accent fill per plate, picked by the owner from six; ink text on it.
Controls are large and outlined or filled, never bare glyphs.
iOS behaviour, the app's own look.

rules.name: The One Fill Per Plate Rule
rules.body: A plate carries at most one accent fill: the thing to act on now. A screen may hold several accent plates (one per routine, one per gym day), never two fills inside one plate.

rules.name: The Ink On Accent Rule
rules.body: Anything on an accent fill is `accent-ink`, and the fill is framed by an ink ring 4px inside its edge, 2px wide (`--accent-ring`). This is what keeps all six accents legible.

rules.name: The Semantic Colours Stay Put Rule
rules.body: Done is green, delete is coral, drill colours label daily routines. The accent never stands in for done, and green never stands in for the accent.

rules.name: The Three Weights Rule
rules.body: Weights are 500, 700 and 900 only, always through `--app-weight-text`, `--app-weight-strong`, `--app-weight-heavy`. Nothing thinner than 500 exists.

rules.name: The Heavy Floor Rule
rules.body: 900 is used only from 17px up. Below that, emphasis is 700.

rules.name: The Quiet Unit Rule
rules.body: Next to a heavy number, its unit and × are smaller (15px), 500, and secondary ("70 × 8" reads as two numbers). On the accent plate the unit stays ink, at 15px 700.

rules.name: The Keyline Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 2px keyline or the ground showing between plates. No drop shadow, glow or backdrop blur.

dos: Do use the tokens in `src/theme.css`; hex values live there only (enforced by test).
Do set weights through the three weight tokens, and use 900 only from 17px up.
Do give each plate at most one accent fill, with ink text and the accent ring.
Do make every control at least 48px (44pt minimum tap area), and give −/+ outlined buttons, not bare glyphs.
Do set units and × as quiet units beside heavy numbers.
Do draw and check every screen at 375×647 first.
Do mark the one plate that matters without acting with the sign-white keyline.
donts: Don't use weights below 500, or any numeric `font-weight` in feature CSS.
Don't put white text on an accent fill, or use the accent for done or delete.
Don't use drop shadows, glows or backdrop blur; depth is keyline and tone.
Don't add a `max-height` media query or shrink anything for short screens.
Don't use drill colours outside daily routines.
Don't use the tertiary label for readable text; it is for disabled and future things.
Don't build a light mode; the app is always dark.
